description: Search the Handshakr suppliers an AI agent may read, by keyword, optionally narrowed by the register's three classifications: `category` (what they do: a top category slug such as 'software-engineering', or a subcategory), `industry` (who it's for, e.g. 'legal-technology') and `delivery` ('software', 'services' or 'hardware'), combined with AND. A classification only narrows the results; it never changes which supplier comes first (contactable first, then by name). Returns name, slug, category, location, description, `contactable` (true only for suppliers who have switched agent access on, the only ones an agent may approach) and `classification`: { what_they_do, who_its_for, delivery } each { slug, top_slug, name, method, method_label, source } or null with `unknown_reason` saying why, and `taxonomy_version`. `method` is supplier, label, sic (Companies House SIC code) or website (their own website text, not reviewed). Claimed suppliers who have not consented are not returned. `description` and `category` are the company's own words or null; text Handshakr wrote from public sources is in `handshakr_summary` / `handshakr_category`, labelled, and is not a fact about the company. `trust_score` is null: no score is computed.

category.description: Optional. What they do: a category slug (e.g. 'software-engineering', 'it-services', or a subcategory such as 'managed-it-services'). A value that is not a category slug is matched against the listing's category label instead, as before.

delivery.description: Optional. How it is delivered: software, services or hardware.

industry.description: Optional. Who it's for: an industry slug (e.g. 'legal-technology', 'healthcare-life-sciences').

limit.description: Maximum number of suppliers to return (1 to 50, default 10).

query.description: Search term matched against seller name and description.

name: search_sellers
title: Search sellers
